ALIEN PHOBIA - FUNCTIONAL TURBO PASCAL REBUILD
================================================

Functional decompilation of Alien Phobia v1.1 by Wah-Software.
This is a standalone source rebuild, not a byte-matching reproduction.
The exact original compiler version is unknown.

All sources and game data live in this directory. Run the executable with this directory as the current directory.

BUILD UNDER MS-DOS
------------------
Requirements:
  * MS-DOS or a DOSBox-X DOS session.
  * Turbo Pascal 7.0 DOS compiler (TPC.EXE), TURBO.TPL and standard units.
    Supply your own compiler; it is not included.
  * A 286 or later CPU for the generated instructions, VGA graphics,
    and sufficient free conventional memory for the compiler and game.
  * Optional Sound Blaster audio: an XMS driver such as HIMEM.SYS,
    at least 190 KB free XMS, and a correct BLASTER environment variable.

The rebuild has been tested with DOSBox-X, not physical DOS hardware.

Example compiler installation:
  C:\TP\BIN\TPC.EXE
  C:\TP\BIN\TURBO.TPL
  C:\TP\UNITS\... (standard units, if installed separately)

Put this repository's files in a DOS directory such as C:\PHOBIA.
At the DOS prompt, type:

  C:
  CD \PHOBIA
  SET TP=C:\TP
  BUILD

BUILD.BAT defaults to C:\TP if TP is unset. TP is the directory containing
BIN and UNITS, without a trailing backslash. Use DOS 8.3 paths without
spaces. Run BUILD from the directory containing PHOBIA.PAS.

To compile manually without the batch file, type this single line:

  C:\TP\BIN\TPC.EXE PHOBIA.PAS /B /TC:\TP\BIN /UC:\TP\UNITS

Replace each C:\TP if your compiler is elsewhere. /B rebuilds required
units, /T locates TURBO.TPL, and /U locates units. USES clauses determine
the compilation order. No separate linker command is needed. Success
produces PHOBIA.EXE and .TPU files in this directory.

Python, MSYS2, Watcom, objdiff and host build tools are not required.

RUN
---
First try:

  PHOBIA NOSOUND

For Sound Blaster audio, enable XMS and set BLASTER to match your hardware
or emulator. Example for port 220, IRQ 7, DMA 1 and HDMA 5:

  SET BLASTER=A220 I7 D1 H5
  PHOBIA

Use settings appropriate to your card. The game can fall back to the PC
speaker when initialization fails. NOSOUND is accepted as either the
first or second command-line argument.

Known limitation: during packaging, the clean DOS build and NOSOUND
60-frame smoke run passed, but the sound-enabled smoke run exited before
writing its completion marker. The cause has not been diagnosed. Use
NOSOUND for now; complete sound-enabled gameplay is not verified.

Controls:
  Left/Right arrows: rotate
  Up arrow: thrust
  Enter: fire
  Scroll Lock: end the round
  Score screen: enter a name when prompted; D quits, N starts another round

ALIEN.DA1 stores high scores and is modified when saving. Back it up if
you want to preserve the initial scores.

Optional bounded smoke run:

  PHOBIA NOSOUND /SMOKE

This runs at least 60 gameplay frames, then enters the score screen.
Press D to finish. Success writes GAME.RES with PASS 0000:380A and the
frame count. This is a smoke test, not exhaustive gameplay validation.

FILES
-----
PHOBIA.PAS   Main program
FAPP.PAS     Initialization, resources and game loop
FCORE.PAS    Game state, movement, collision, rendering and effects
FGFX.PAS     Graphics allocation and palette fading
FHW.PAS      Sound Blaster, DMA and mixer
FINPUT.PAS   Keyboard interrupt handler and video helpers
FRECOVER.PAS Resource, string, environment and other recovered helpers
FSCORES.PAS  High-score display, entry and persistence
FSOUND.PAS   Sample loading and XMS streaming
RXMS.PAS     XMS interface
*.DAT        Original graphics, palettes and audio
ALIEN.DA1    Original initial high scores
FILE_ID.DIZ  Original game identification
BUILD.BAT    Manual MS-DOS build
README.md    GitHub landing page
NOTICE.TXT   Provenance and licensing status
STATUS.TXT   Recovery accounting when packaged
MANIFEST.TXT SHA-256 hashes of packaged files

# Lemmings in HTML-in-Canvas

A modern, WebGL-enhanced reconstruction of the classic Lemmings game using the experimental **HTML-in-Canvas** API (`layoutsubtree`, `drawElementImage`, `onpaint`). 

In this implementation, each Lemming is a real `<div>` child of a `<canvas>` element. This creates a DOM-based Entity-Component-System (ECS) where entities are rendered directly into the canvas every frame while retaining native mouse hit-testing and accessibility support on the drawn pixels.

**▶ [Play now](https://vorticoncmdr.github.io/lemmings/)** — requires Chrome 148 to 154 with `chrome://flags/#canvas-draw-element` enabled (see [Runtime Requirement](#️-runtime-requirement) below).

---

## 💚 Special thank you to
- ccexplore & rt for sharing their knowledge on [Lemmings Archive](https://www.camanis.net/lemmings/tools.php)
- [Mindless](https://github.com/carlreinke/lemmings-tools)
- [Lemmings Forum](https://www.lemmingsforums.net/) for keeping the game alive
- crisp for the OG [dhtml Lemmings](https://www.elizium.nu/scripts/lemmings/)
- [trufae](https://github.com/trufae/fxos-app-lemmings) for preserving DHTML Lemmings on Github
- the [Lemmings Level Database](https://lldb.camanis.net/) where I found the 2-player levels
- [oklemenz](https://github.com/oklemenz/LemmingsJS/tree/master) for LemmingsJS
- amiga protracker module player for web audio api (c) 2012-2013 firehawk/tda

---

## Motivation
I wanted to level up my agent coding skills and how to better learn than to practise? After recently reading about HTML-in-canvas I thought this might be something interesting to target and since I love playing Lemmings, DHTML Lemmings came to mind.

I really didn't expect to release something since Lemmings in HTML & canvas isn't exactly ground breaking but I soon discovered that there are still treasures buried in this old game.

There was no reconstruction of the EGA, CGA or Tandy version and no 2-player mode (which didn't exist in the DOS version)

---

## ⚠️ Runtime Requirement

The experimental HTML-in-Canvas API is in [origin trial](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/html-in-canvas-origin-trial#limitations) and needs **Chrome 148 to 154**. It will not run on standard browsers, Safari, or Firefox (which will display an unsupported banner).

To run this project:
1. Use **Chrome 148 to 154** (or a Chromium build supporting the flag).
2. Navigate to `chrome://flags/#canvas-draw-element`.
3. Set the flag to **Enabled** and restart the browser.

---

## 🚀 Running the Project

This project is fully client-side, bundled/served via [Vite](https://vitejs.dev):

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the printed `http://localhost:5173` URL in Chrome with the flag enabled.

For a production build (a `dist/` folder ready to serve statically, e.g. on GitHub Pages):

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview   # serve dist/ locally to sanity-check the build
```

---

## 🎮 Features

### 1. Single Player Mode
- **346 Playable Levels**: Every rating from the original DOS *Lemmings*, *Oh No! More Lemmings*, and the Holiday/Xmas Lemmings packs (`Fun`/`Tricky`/`Taxing`/`Mayhem`, `Crazy`/`Wild`/`Wicked`/`Havoc`/`Tame`, `Flurry`/`Blizzard` '93 & '94, `Frost`, `Hail`, `Xmas` '91 & '92) plus a 20-level Amiga `2-player` pack.
- **Live `.DAT` Decoding**: Terrain, placed objects, steel areas, and level metadata for *every* rating, including `2-player`, are decoded directly from the original DOS/Amiga binary files (`gamedata/<pack>/LEVEL<n>.DAT`, `gamedata/Amiga-Two-Player/Level NN.lvl`, etc.) in the browser at play time — no offline conversion step. See [`docs/gamedata.md`](docs/gamedata.md).
- **8 Original Skills**: Full state machine implementations for Climber, Floater, Bomber (Exploder), Blocker, Builder, Basher, Miner, and Digger.
- **Classic UI & Controls**: Interactive skill toolbar with skill counters, release-rate controllers (+/-), fast-forward (4x speed), pause, and a "nuke" button.
- **EGA / CGA / Tandy Video Modes**: A pause-menu "Video Mode" setting recolors terrain, objects, and the lemming sprites themselves to match real EGA (per-level palette), CGA (native 2bpp, `lemmings` pack), or Tandy (fixed hardware palette, `lemmings`/`oh-no-more-lemmings`) hardware output — VGA stays the default fixed palette. CGA "special" (`VGASPEC`-backed) levels are decoded via their own native `CGASPEC<n>.DAT` art rather than re-quantizing VGA art.
- **4 Music Engines + Real DOS Sound Effects**: A "Music Engine" setting switches between the Amiga ProTracker rotation, real per-pack AdLib (OPL2) music decoded from `ADLIB.DAT`, pre-rendered MP3 tracks, and real per-pack Tandy 3-voice PSG music decoded from `TANDYSND.DAT`.

### 2. 2-Player Lockstep Multiplayer
- **P2P Connection**: Direct peer-to-peer multiplayer using WebRTC data channels via [PeerJS](https://peerjs.com/).
- **Lockstep Synchronization**: A fully synchronized local simulation. Instead of sharing state variables for hundreds of entities, peers exchange only tick-stamped player commands.
- **Input Delay Buffer**: Commands are queued and executed with a fixed buffer (`INPUT_DELAY_TICKS = 6` ticks, ~480ms) to hide network latency and keep the simulations perfectly aligned.

### 3. Level Editor
- **Live Terrain/Object Palette**: Stamp and Objects tools are decoded straight from the original `GROUND<n>O.DAT`/`VGAGR<n>.DAT` graphic-style files — no baked tile catalog. Placed pieces are real interactive HTML-in-Canvas entities (native click/drag hit-testing via `drawElementImage`), the same ECS pattern used for lemmings and decorations in real gameplay.
- **Grid Painting**: Interactive canvas interface to paint terrain semantic values directly (Air, Soft, Soft Right, Soft Left, Steel, Water, Fire, Exit, Slicer).
- **Smart Brushes**: An Exit tool that paints tall columns to ensure walking Lemmings collide with the exit trigger (sampled at mid-body, y+16).
- **Level Configurations**: Configure starting parameters such as skill availability counts, release rates, saved percentage targets, time limits, and music.
- **Local Storage**: Saves, loads, and manages draft playtests and custom levels in `localStorage` under `lemmings.customLevels.v1`.
- **Export/Import Real DOS Levels**: "Export Level Pack…"/"Import Level…" convert custom levels to/from real, LZ-compressed DOS `LEVEL*.DAT` files, playable in an actual DOSBox install. See [`docs/level-export-import.md`](docs/level-export-import.md).

### 4. Custom Graphics Pack Editor
- **`graphicspack.html`**: A standalone tool to author your own DOS-compatible ground/object graphics sets — import/quantize your own art or clone an existing pack, hand-edit on a palette-constrained pixel canvas (pencil/eraser/bucket/eyedropper), and manage object animation frames/trigger boxes.
- **Real Export**: Saves for use with this project's own editor/game, or exports as real `GROUND<n>O.DAT`/`VGAGR<n>.DAT` files for a genuine DOSBox pack folder. See [`docs/graphics-pack-editor.md`](docs/graphics-pack-editor.md).

### 5. Deterministic Replay, Rewind & Cheats
- **Input Logging**: Every simulation-affecting input (skill selection, release rate adjustments, nuking) is recorded along with the simulation tick it occurred on.
- **URL-based Sharing**: Replay records are compressed, encoded, and appended to the URL (`?replay=...`). The result page offers a "Copy replay link" button to share playthroughs.
- **Rewind**: A scrub bar (next to Pause/Fast-Forward) jumps the simulation to an earlier tick by restoring a snapshot and headlessly fast-forwarding the command log back to it — non-destructive while watching a replay, a true rewind/retry while playing live. See [`docs/rewind.md`](docs/rewind.md).
- **Debugging Cheats**: Appending `?cheat=1` to the URL loads the level with 99 of every skill available for sandbox testing.

### 6. WebGL Shaders & Visual FX
- **CRT Simulation**: CRT filter overlay including scanlines and vignette shading.
- **GL Shimmer & Lighting**: WebGL fragment shaders (`src/webgl-effects.js`, `src/lighting.js`) that sample the rendered canvas to create shimmery liquid surfaces and lighting calculations.
- **Screen FX**: Skill-triggered WebGL screen distortions — bomber shockwave/shake, basher chromatic aberration, miner jitter, digger squish, blocker shield shimmer, floater turbulence, builder holographic mesh — plus a secret Shift+D tuning popover for live-adjusting effect parameters. See [`docs/screen-fx.md`](docs/screen-fx.md).
- **Hover Highlight**: The Lemming currently hovered by the mouse pointer while a skill is armed is recolored with the same red tint 2-player mode uses for team 1.
- **Particle System**: Exploding sparks and liquid particles rendered directly onto the canvas view. See [`docs/particle-system.md`](docs/particle-system.md).

### 7. Headless Level Solver
- **`solver.html`**: Pick any level and run a headless, best-effort **Monte Carlo Tree Search** (`src/solver.js`) for a skill-assignment sequence that solves it — no Canary/flag needed to search, only to watch the resulting replay. See [`docs/solver.md`](docs/solver.md).

### 8. Amiga ProTracker Audio Engine
- **Chiptune Synthesis**: Custom Amiga audio tracker player synthesized in JavaScript (`src/AmigaAudioEngine.js`) to play retro music formats.
- **Original SFX**: Reuses digital audio files (`upgrade/lemmings/sounds/*.ogg`) for classic sound cues ("Let's Go!", "Oh No!", splats, explosions, and tools).

---

## 📂 Directory Structure

```
├── src/                  # Modern ES Module codebase (JS + game.css) — no build-time deps beyond Vite
├── assets/               # First-party static assets the live game fetches directly: UI chrome
│                         # (skill toolbar/control-bar icon strips, background.png), the menu's
│                         # handwriting-style font, and the editor's custom cursor SVGs
├── gamedata/             # Original DOS/Amiga game packs (LEVEL*.DAT, GROUND*O.DAT, VGAGR*.DAT,
│                         # MAIN.DAT, VGASPEC*.DAT, ADLIB.DAT, TANDYSND.DAT, ...), fully committed
│                         # to this repo — live-decoded at play time/edit time for every rating,
│                         # including gamedata/Amiga-Two-Player/ (2-player's raw *.lvl source).
│                         # See docs/gamedata.md and docs/2-player-dos-assets.md.
├── levels/               # Shared object/decoration art (levels/{gfx,ani,doors,traps}/*.gif) +
│                         # levels/music/*.ogg (unused leftover, see CLAUDE.md)
├── logos/                # Result-screen rating badge art (complete/failed/holiday93/holiday94/...)
├── upgrade/<pack>/       # Optional, non-vanilla polish grouped by gamedata pack (see CLAUDE.md):
│                         # backgrounds/*.webp, lemmings/sounds/*.ogg (shared SFX), <pack>/music/
├── graphics_tools/       # Node scripts used to reverse-engineer/verify the binary formats above
│                         # (render_*.js/.mjs previews, parity_check_phase*.mjs, lem_decompress.js)
├── vite-plugins/         # Custom Vite plugins (gamedataDirListing.js — see vite.config.js)
├── scripts/              # One-off maintenance shell scripts (e.g. convert-backgrounds-to-webp.sh)
├── docs/                 # Binary format specs + architecture notes — see "Documentation Reference"
├── index.html            # Main menu, level selector, and Level Editor mount
├── game.html             # Main gameplay viewport and multiplayer lobby mount
└── *.html                # Standalone dev tools in the root — see "Developer Tools" below
```

---

## 🛠️ Codebase Architecture

The modern ported game is organized as a collection of ES modules located under the `src/` folder — no vendored third-party engine code, everything below is native:

### Core Application
- **`index.html`** / **`src/menuMain.js`**: Initial entry page. Sets up the main menu, difficulty level selector, custom level manager, and initializes the Level Editor.
- **`game.html`** / **`src/gameMain.js`**: Handles the main gameplay view, runs the fixed 80ms simulation step loop (`TICK_SECONDS = 0.08`), and coordinates WebRTC lobby connections.
- **`src/entities.js`**: Contains the Entity-Component-System (ECS) engine. Implements the 8 skill state machines, coordinate systems, step-up (≤12px) / step-down (≤8px) walking geometry, and coordinate checks. The state machine itself (`stepLemming`/`applyJob`) is DOM-free — DOM writes and sound playback are separated out (`syncEntityVisuals`, `stepLemming`'s returned `sounds` array) so it's callable headlessly, e.g. for the rewind feature's fast-forward. See [`docs/rewind.md`](docs/rewind.md).
- **`src/terrain.js`**: Manages the level collision matrix (mapped onto a grid of 0-9 values). Manages drawing the offscreen canvas where Digger, Basher, and Miner actions physically carve paths or Builders place stairs. `snapshot()`/`restore()` bundle both for the rewind feature.
- **`src/leveldata.js`**: `loadLevelDef()` is the single entry point `gameMain.js` calls to load a level for every rating; it dispatches to `gamedataLevelLoader.js`, which live-decodes all of them (including `2-player`). Also owns Run-Length Encoding (RLE) grid compression/decompression, load-bearing for the level editor's custom-level storage format.
- **`src/gamedataLevelLoader.js`**: Live-decodes a real level directly from `gamedata/<pack>/LEVEL<n>.DAT` (or `DLVEL<n>.DAT` for Oh No! More Lemmings) for the 6 DOS packs, and from `gamedata/Amiga-Two-Player/Level NN.lvl` for `2-player` — terrain-piece/object/steel-area placement and metadata — using native `src/levelReader.js`/`src/groundReader.js`/`src/vgaspecReader.js`/`src/oddTableReader.js`, and bakes the result into one shared `levelDef` shape the rest of the engine needs no awareness of which pipeline produced. See [`docs/gamedata.md`](docs/gamedata.md) / [`docs/2-player-dos-assets.md`](docs/2-player-dos-assets.md).
- **`src/gamedataPacks.js`**: Shared per-pack table (filename casing, level-file prefix, which graphic styles/ODDTABLE/VGASPEC a pack ships, and the `rating → {pack, config.json group}` mapping) used by every live-decode module.
- **`src/groundCatalog.js`** / **`src/groundReader.js`**: Live-decode a graphic style's terrain-piece bitmaps and object animation strips from `GROUND<n>O.DAT`/`VGAGR<n>.DAT` — shared by the level editor's palette, the graphics pack editor, and `gamedataLevelLoader.js`.
- **`src/vgaspecReader.js`** / **`src/cgaspecReader.js`**: Decode `VGASPEC<n>.DAT`/`CGASPEC<n>.DAT`-backed "special" levels — a fully custom background image instead of tiled ground pieces — for VGA/EGA and CGA video modes respectively.
- **`src/lemmingSpriteCatalog.js`**: Recolors lemming sprites for the EGA/CGA/Tandy Video Mode settings from real per-level/hardware palettes (VGA stays the fixed default palette).
- **`src/decorations.js`**: Manages non-terrain interactive and animated game decorations (e.g., animated entrance hatches, exits, and traps) as real HTML-in-Canvas ECS entities. Decompresses animated GIF frames via WebCodecs (`ImageDecoder`) into custom offscreen sprite strips to guarantee synchronization with the simulation ticks.

### Multiplayer & Controls
- **`src/network.js`**: Interfaces PeerJS/WebRTC. Manages connection heartbeats, packet routing, and connection watchdogs.
- **`src/editor.js`** / **`src/editorHistory.js`**: The painting loop, palette options, mouse brushes, undo/redo history, and validation rules for the custom Level Editor. Placed pieces/objects/steel areas are real HTML-in-Canvas ECS entities, not flat canvas drawing.
- **`src/editorBake.js`** / **`src/levelBakeGeometry.js`**: Turn the editor's placed-piece lists (or a live-decoded gamedata level) into the flat terrain bitmap + collision grid + `levelImages`/`traps` real gameplay consumes.
- **`src/datLevelEncoder.js`** / **`src/exportDat.js`** / **`src/importDat.js`**: Convert custom levels to/from real, LZ-compressed DOS Lemmings `LEVEL*.DAT` files — "Export Level Pack…"/"Import Level…" in the My Levels screen. See [`docs/level-export-import.md`](docs/level-export-import.md).
- **`graphicspack.html`** / **`src/graphicsPackMain.js`** / **`src/groundSetFormat.js`** / **`src/customGraphicsPacks.js`**: Standalone custom graphics pack (ground/object set) authoring tool — paint/import/clone art, then either save it for use in this project's own editor/game (IndexedDB) or export real DOS-compatible `GROUND<n>O.DAT`/`VGAGR<n>.DAT` files. See [`docs/graphics-pack-editor.md`](docs/graphics-pack-editor.md).
- **`src/replay.js`**: Handles compressing/decompressing user inputs into URL parameters.
- **`src/solver.js`**: Headless, best-effort level solver (`solver.html`/`src/solverMain.js`) — re-simulates a level off-DOM using an event-driven Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) that branches at genuine decision points (spawn, wall, gap, trap) and hands back a replay command log for the best attempt found. See [`docs/solver.md`](docs/solver.md).
- **`src/rewind.js`** / **`src/worldSnapshot.js`**: Reverse playback / rewind — jump the live simulation or a loaded replay to an earlier tick by restoring a one-time snapshot and headlessly fast-forwarding the recorded command log back to the target tick. A "Rewind" scrub bar in the skill toolbar; non-destructive while watching a replay, a true rewind/retry (discards what was going to happen next) during live play. See [`docs/rewind.md`](docs/rewind.md).
- **`src/ui.js`** / **`src/debugPanel.js`** / **`src/effectsTuning.js`**: Toolbar renderers, keyboard shortcuts (1-8 for skills, Escape to pause, Arrow keys for rate/volume), the pause menu's full settings surface (CRT/Lighting/Particles/Screen FX/Background, Music Engine, Video Mode), and a secret Shift+D popover for live-tuning Screen FX shader parameters.
- **`src/settings.js`**: Wraps `localStorage` to persist volume levels, sound/music toggles, particle settings, and shader states.
- **`src/progress.js`** / **`src/progressMp.js`**: Level unlock trackers in `localStorage`.

### Audio & Visuals
- **`src/sound.js`** / **`src/musicManager.js`**: Controls HTML5 audio playback and connects the tracker/hardware audio engines. `musicManager.js` switches live between 4 Music Engines: the shared Amiga ProTracker `.mod` rotation, real per-pack AdLib (OPL2) music decoded from `ADLIB.DAT`, pre-rendered per-pack `.mp3` tracks, and real per-pack Tandy 3-voice PSG music decoded from `TANDYSND.DAT`. See [`docs/music-engine-naming.md`](docs/music-engine-naming.md).
- **`src/AmigaAudioEngine.js`** / **`src/gamedataMusicPlayer.js`** / **`src/oplAudioEngine.js`** / **`src/tandyAudioEngine.js`**: Low-level audio synthesis — the Amiga ProTracker player, the AdLib/OPL2 driver (also the source of `sfx-explorer.html`'s sound effects, `src/dosSfxMapping.js`), and a from-scratch Tandy 1000 PSG driver port (`src/tandySfxMapping.js`; see [`docs/SOUND_FORMAT.md`](docs/SOUND_FORMAT.md) / [`docs/SOUND_FORMAT_ADLIB.md`](docs/SOUND_FORMAT_ADLIB.md)).
- **`src/webgl-effects.js`**: WebGL-based visual shader processors (shimmers, reflections, CRT scanlines, Screen FX distortions), tuned by a family of `src/*Tuning.js` files (`crtTuning.js`, `waterTuning.js`, `lavaTuning.js`, `foamTuning.js`, `sandTuning.js`, `moltenTuning.js`, `iceFloeTuning.js`, `throwerTuning.js`, `lightingTuning.js`, `particlesTuning.js`) backing the Shift+D debug popover above.
- **`src/lighting.js`**: WebGL effects for active entities and shadows.
- **`src/particles.js`** / **`src/fireworks.js`**: Simulation of explosion fragments and fireworks. See [`docs/particle-system.md`](docs/particle-system.md).
- **`src/colorPalette.js`** / **`src/imageQuantizer.js`** / **`src/planarImage.js`** / **`src/binaryReader.js`** / **`src/datContainer.js`** / **`src/datContainerCompressor.js`** / **`src/mainDatCatalog.js`**: Shared low-level building blocks (palette handling, image quantization for custom-art import, planar bitplane decode, binary stream reading, DOS `.DAT` container packing/unpacking, `MAIN.DAT` asset catalog) used across the live-decode and dev-tool code paths.

---

## 🛠️ Developer Tools & Utilities

The project includes several standalone pages (accessible in the root directory, all wired into `vite.config.js`'s build) designed to examine, author, and process original Lemmings/Oh No! More Lemmings game assets:

- **`explorer.html` (DOS Lemmings Asset Explorer)**: A web-based inspector to load and visualize graphics, palettes, levels, and animations decoded live from the original MS-DOS/Amiga `.DAT`/`.lvl` files. See [`docs/explorer.md`](docs/explorer.md).
- **`converter.html` (GFX & Level Converter)**: No longer a required build step — real gameplay and the level editor both live-decode terrain/objects directly now for every rating. Kept as a standalone tool to export a portable snapshot of a level. See [`docs/converter.md`](docs/converter.md).
- **`graphicspack.html` (Graphics Pack Editor)**: Author custom DOS-compatible ground/object graphics sets — paint on a palette-constrained pixel canvas, manage object animation frames/trigger boxes, save for use in this project or export real `GROUND<n>O.DAT`/`VGAGR<n>.DAT` files. See [`docs/graphics-pack-editor.md`](docs/graphics-pack-editor.md).
- **`sprite-editor.html` (Sprite Editor)**: A specialized paint program to modify pixel sheets, set anchor offsets, and test individual frame sequences. See [`docs/sprite-editor.md`](docs/sprite-editor.md).
- **`gif2sprite.html` (GIF to Spritesheet Converter)**: Converts standard multi-frame animated GIFs into linear horizontal sprite strips suitable for standard CSS step-animations. See [`docs/gif2sprite.md`](docs/gif2sprite.md).
- **`solver.html` (Level Solver)**: Pick a level and it runs a headless, best-effort Monte Carlo Tree Search (`src/solver.js`) for a skill-assignment sequence that solves it, then offers a "Watch replay" link into `game.html`. No Canary/flag needed to search — only to watch the result play out. See [`docs/solver.md`](docs/solver.md).
- **`assembly.html` (Exploded Assembly Viewer)**: Loads a real DOS level straight from `gamedata/` and flies every terrain/object piece into place — a dev viewer sharing its live-decode core with `game.html`'s between-levels piece-flying screen. See [`docs/assembly.md`](docs/assembly.md).
- **`sfx-explorer.html` (DOS Sound Effect Explorer)**: Plays each pack's real, live-decoded AdLib/Tandy sound effects side-by-side with the current `upgrade/lemmings/sounds/*.ogg` set, for building/confirming a name↔index mapping by ear.
- **`missing.html` (Missing Upgrades)**: An asset-coverage audit — checks every optional `upgrade/` asset (backgrounds/sounds/music) against what's actually on disk and reports what's still missing, with a direct `game.html` link for every catalog level (including no-title ones, dimmed).
- **`graphics_tools/`**: Node scripts (not browser pages) used to reverse-engineer and cross-verify the binary formats above against real DOS asset dumps — per-format `render_*.js`/`.mjs` previews and `parity_check_phase*.mjs` regression checks; `graphics_tools/sound_dispatch_explorer.html` is one further, standalone `CGALEMMI.EXE` sound-dispatch research artifact.

---

## 📜 Documentation Reference

The `docs/` directory has both architecture notes and binary format specs:
- `docs/gamedata.md`: Which `gamedata/` packs back which ratings, filename-casing gotchas, and how live decoding works end to end.
- `docs/2-player-dos-assets.md`: How `2-player` came to fully live-decode from its raw Amiga `.lvl` source, reusing the `lemmings` pack's own (byte-identical) ground/object art.

- `docs/graphics-pack-editor.md`: The custom graphics-pack authoring tool's format/verification writeup, including two real decoder bugs found and fixed along the way.
- `docs/level-export-import.md`: Exporting custom levels to real, LZ-compressed DOS `LEVEL*.DAT` files and importing them back — byte-level field mapping, unit-conversion gotchas, and bugs found/fixed along the way.
- `docs/rewind.md`: How the lemming state machine became headless-callable, the terrain/world snapshot primitives, and the reverse-playback/rewind feature built on top — live vs. replay semantics, the benchmark behind skipping a keyframe cache, and how it was verified.
- `docs/music-engine-naming.md`: The `upgrade/<pack>/music/track-NN.{mod,mp3}` naming convention the Amiga/MP3 music engines expect, and each pack's real track count.
- `docs/solver.md`: How the headless level solver's MCTS search/rollout policy works, its known limitations, and how it was verified.
- `docs/screen-fx.md`: The skill-triggered WebGL Screen FX distortions — design choices and the debug-popover tuning surface.
- `docs/particle-system.md`: Current state of the environmental particle system and its related shader effects.
- `docs/assembly.md`: The exploded-assembly dev viewer and the game's shared level-prepare/piece-flying screen.

# Civilization (1991, v475.01) — recompiled to C

This directory turns the original DOS `CIV.EXE` (plus its overlays and the
MGRAPHIC / sound drivers) into C source that builds natively for Linux
(SDL2) and for DOS (DJGPP).  The original game files are still needed at
run time (graphics, text, and the program image itself).

**The generated source is derived from your copy of the game. Keep it
private; do not redistribute it.**

## Running

    make                 # builds ./civ (needs gcc, SDL2, zlib)
    ./civ                # reads civ.cfg: 1920x1080, widescreen, fullscreen

Useful options (all also valid in `civ.cfg` as `name = value`):

| option | meaning |
|---|---|
| `--res 1920x1080` | window / screen size |
| `--fullscreen` | fullscreen (Alt+Enter toggles) |
| `--widescreen` | wider map view filling the screen (square pixels) |
| `--classic` | original 320x200, letterboxed at 4:3 |
| `--zoom N` | widescreen: screen pixels per game pixel (default height/200) |
| `--mapwidth N` | world width in squares, even, 80 (original) to 160; height stays 50 |
| `--realtime` | turns pass on a clock (see below) |
| `--turnsecs S` | realtime: seconds per turn (default 3) |
| `--barbarians 0` | no barbarians: no raids, uprisings or barbarians from huts |
| `--rankings 0` | no historians' reports (wealthiest, largest ... civilizations); always off in multiplayer |
| `--sound none\|speaker` | sound driver (AdLib emulation is not implemented yet) |
| `--setup` | ask the original graphics / sound / mouse questions |
| `--gamedir DIR` | where the original files are |

Widescreen at 1920x1080 gives a 384x216 game screen at 5x: the map view is
19x13 squares instead of 15x12.  Other screens (city, reports, intro) keep
their 320x200 layout and are shown centred.

`make run` builds and starts the game.

## Added features

* **Produce gold** — in a city's "What shall we build" list (CHANGE on the
  city screen, or when production is due) pick **Gold: production to
  treasury**; picking anything else from the list switches it off again.
  The GOLD button (bottom right of the city screen, next to EXIT) and the
  **G** key toggle it too.  While it is on ("GOLD!") the city's production
  goes into your treasury each turn instead of the production box, so
  nothing gets built.  The setting is saved with the game (`CIVILn.NAT`
  next to `CIVILn.SVE`).
* **Auto-work settlers** — press **A** on an active Settlers unit.  It
  improves the 21 squares of the nearest own city (within 2 squares), or
  the 5x5 squares around it: road, then railroad, then irrigation (not on
  forest, swamp or jungle, where irrigating changes the terrain).  Orders
  the game refuses (no Railroad yet, no water nearby) are skipped and
  retried in a later pass once new work has been done.  Press any key while
  the settlers are active to take control back.

* **Mouse wheel zoom** (widescreen) — on the map, the wheel changes the
  size of a game pixel: at 1920x1080 5x (19x13 squares), 4x (25x16) or 3x
  (35x22).  The view never gets wider than half the world.
* **Drag-scroll** — drag the map with the left (or right) button; a click
  without moving still goes to the game as before.  Zoom and scrolling are
  applied while the game waits for your orders.

* **Real-time mode** (`realtime = 1`) — time passes even when you do
  nothing: each turn lasts a few seconds (default 3) and then ends by
  itself, the other civilizations move and the year advances.  Units with
  goto orders (**G**, then click the destination) walk on every turn, so
  fast units cover more ground than slow ones.  **Tab** switches to the next
  unit, **clicking** one of your units makes it the active one (cancelling
  its standing orders).  **[** / **-** slower, **]** / **=** faster, **F12**
  pause.  The bar at the bottom of the status panel shows the turn time.
  Dialogs, menus and city screens stop the clock.  A discovered advance
  is announced with a short message instead of the picture and dialog.
* **Multiplayer over the network** — two PCs on the same network play one
  game in real time.  Choose **Multiplayer** in the start menu: **H** hosts
  a game, **F** searches the network (UDP broadcast) and lists the games
  found; **Enter** joins.  When the other player is in, the host presses
  **Enter** and starts a new game as usual; the joining player gets one of
  the other civilizations.  Both play at the same time; the turn clock (the
  host's `turnsecs`) keeps running; nothing is closed for you: a turn that
  is due ends when you are back on the map (while the host has a city
  screen or dialog open, the host's game waits there).  Ports: TCP 28400, UDP 28401.  Both need the same
  `mapwidth`.

  How it works: the host's game is the real one.  At every turn start it
  sends the game state (the game's own save data plus the map) to the other
  PC, whose player plays on it at the same time.  The orders given there
  (unit moves and orders, goto targets, city builds, gold settings, tax
  and science rates, research goal) are
  sent to the host twice a second.  When the host's turn clock runs out,
  the units on both PCs are done; the other PC sends its last orders at
  once and the host carries them out in the same turn, so what was done
  there stays.  You stay on the map (or in your city screen) until the next
  state arrives (a player in a city screen or dialog is not waited for;
  their later orders count for the next turn).  Diplomacy of the joining
  player's civilization is still decided by the computer.
* **Wider worlds** — `--mapwidth 160` (or `mapwidth = 160` in `civ.cfg`)
  makes the world up to twice as wide; it still wraps east-west.  New
  random worlds use the whole width (land amount scales with it), AI
  civilizations start anywhere, and EARTH is stretched to the chosen width.
  The minimap shows an 80 column window that follows the view; the world
  map and the end-of-game replay show 80 columns around your capital.
  Saved games of a wider world need the same `--mapwidth` to load (the map
  layers are in `CIVILn.WMP` next to the save) and can't be loaded by the
  original game.

Code: `src/native/capital.c`, `src/native/autowork.c`, `src/native/mapnav.c`,
`src/native/mapsize.c` (wide map support), `src/native/realtime.c`,
`src/native/mp.c` and `mp_net.c` (multiplayer), overlay drawing in
`src/native/overlay.c`; the hook points are in `tools/hooks.txt`.

## DOS build

    make dos             # -> civ.exe (DPMI host embedded, no CWSDPMI.EXE needed)

Uses the DJGPP cross compiler in `toolchain/djgpp` (prebuilt GCC 12.2 from
github.com/andrewwutw/build-djgpp) and CWSDPMI from delorie.com, both
downloaded into `toolchain/`.  Copy `civ.exe` into the game directory under
another name (e.g. `CIVR.EXE`, the original `CIV.EXE` must stay) and run it.
The DOS build uses real VGA mode 13h and the classic 320x200 layout.

## Layout

    tools/        lifter (x86-16 -> C) and analysis / test tools (Python)
      lift.py       the static recompiler
      seeds.txt     extra code entry points (only reachable via pointers)
      patches.txt   instruction constants, segments and displacements replaced
                    by expressions (widescreen, wider maps)
      hooks.txt     native functions called before given instructions
      overrides.txt lifted functions replaced by hand written C
    src/gen/      generated C, one file per code segment / overlay / driver
    src/native/   hand written replacements of game functions
    runtime/      CPU helpers, DOS/BIOS/VGA/PIT/mouse emulation, native
                  graphics driver (gfx.c), SDL and DOS platform layers,
                  8086 interpreter (fallback + reference)
    tests/        differential test harnesses; tests/scripts: input scripts
                  for the run checks below

`make lift` regenerates `src/gen` from `../CIV` (Python 3 with capstone and
unicorn: `tools/py` points at a virtualenv; recreate it with
`python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install capstone unicorn` and edit
`tools/py`).

## How it works

* `CIV.EXE` is EXEPACK-compressed; the root image, 23 MS-LINK overlays and
  the drivers are disassembled by recursive descent (1258 functions).
* Each function becomes a C function operating on an emulated register file
  and 1 MB of real-mode memory, so behaviour is exactly the original's.
  Flag computations are only emitted where a later instruction reads them,
  and compare+branch pairs become plain C conditions.
* A shadow call stack handles the program's tricks: thunks that pop their
  own return address, `_setargv`/`__chkstk` stack games, self-modifying
  driver thunks (executed through the interpreter), INT 3Fh overlay calls.
* The runtime emulates DOS (files, memory blocks, EXEC 4B03 driver loading,
  FCBs), BIOS (video, keyboard, timer), PIC/PIT/keyboard controller, VGA DAC
  and an INT 33h mouse.
* The MCGA graphics driver is reimplemented natively (`runtime/gfx.c`) so
  screen pages can be any size; in classic mode it can be checked against
  the original driver call by call (`CIV_GFX=shadow`).

## Adding features

Replace a lifted function with C: add its name (e.g. `f_1b05_0004`) to
`tools/overrides.txt`, run `make lift`, and define the function in
`src/native/*.c`.  The original stays callable as `lifted_<name>`; see
`src/native/mapview.c` for an example (arguments via `FARG(n)`, game
variables via `GW()/GB()`, finish with `RET_FAR(0)`).  For single constants
use `tools/patches.txt`.

`tools/dumpfunc.py ../CIV root SEG:OFF` prints the disassembly of a function.

## Testing

    make test       # every distinct instruction vs unicorn (102k cases)
    make functest   # whole pure functions vs unicorn
    tools/compare_runs.sh tests/scripts/monkey1d.txt
                                   # lifted vs interpreter, deterministic trace
    tools/widestore_check.sh       # wide map storage at width 80 vs the original
                                   # layout: game state must be the same
    tools/mp_check.sh              # multiplayer: host + joining game on one PC
    HOSTCIV=3 tools/mp_check.sh    # same test, host plays civ 3
    CIV_GFX=shadow  # native graphics driver vs original, per call

Test runs use a copy of the game in `build/game` (they save games).
`CIV_ORIGINAL=1` leaves the game's menus unchanged (no Multiplayer and Gold
entries), as the comparison runs need.  `CIV_MPDEBUG=1` logs multiplayer
turns and orders.

Debug aids: `CIV_WATCHDOG=N`, `CIV_DUMP=secs`, `CIV_TRACE=file`
(`CIV_TRACE_STACK=1` adds the call stack, lifted runs only), `CIV_ITRACE=n`,
`CIV_MAPTRACE=file` (map square writes), `CIV_GFXDEBUG=1`, `--script FILE`
(see runtime/script.c).  Analysis helpers: `tools/mapscan.py`,
`tools/widthscan.py` (map width constants), `tools/ctxat.sh MOD SEG:OFF`.

## Known limitations

* Widescreen: dialogs over the map are still placed for 320x200 (left of

* No AdLib/Sound Blaster emulation yet (PC speaker works); text-mode setup
  screen is printed to the terminal, not drawn in the window.
* A rare timing-dependent "divide error" was seen once at startup in
  widescreen and could not be reproduced; the message shows a call stack.
* The DOS build compiles and links but could not be run here (DOSBox needs
  a display); untested on real DOS.

# DeDaggerate

Reverse-engineering of Bethesda's 1996 *The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall*,
targeting the original Watcom 10-ish DOS build.

The game ships as two binaries:
- `DAGGER.EXE` — 16-bit launcher program
- `FALL.EXE` — 32-bit LE game/engine binary

The goal of this project is to produce a codebase that can _behaviourally_
replicate these programs in order to open up opportunities for porting and
other projects that benefit from access to a source tree.

This project does _not_ intend to produce a byte-for-byte decompilation.

## Ghidra

Scripts in this section expect you to have `$GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` set to point
at your Ghidra install.

### Setup

Install the required Ghidra extensions:
- [`ghidra-watcom-dos`](https://github.com/DeDaggerate/ghidra-watcom-dos)
provides Watcom compiler/libc support
- [`yetmorecode/ghidra-lx-loader`](https://github.com/yetmorecode/ghidra-lx-loader)
provides LE/LX executable loader

Drop your own copies of `DAGGER.EXE` and `FALL.EXE` into `binaries/`.
Daggerfall has been free for a few years now so it should be easy enough to
get your hands on a copy.

Then run `scripts/bootstrap.py` which will replay all annotations into a Ghidra
project. Then open the generated `ghidra/DeDaggerate.gpr` in Ghidra.

### Generating Annotations

To commit work you've done, export it with `scripts/export.py`. This overwrites
`annotations/DAGGER.EXE.json` and `annotations/FALL.EXE.json` with the current
user-defined markup.

# Civilization (1991) — reconstructed source

A C reconstruction of the DOS game's `CIV.EXE` (see `NOTES.md` for how it was recovered and
verified), with an SDL2 front end that uses the original game files.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![The map](docs/screenshots/map.png) | ![A city](docs/screenshots/city.png) |
| The map | A city |
| ![A city view](docs/screenshots/cityview.png) | ![A discovery](docs/screenshots/discovery.png) |
| A city view | A discovery |
| ![The Civilopedia](docs/screenshots/civilopedia.png) | ![A newspaper](docs/screenshots/newspaper.png) |
| The Civilopedia | A newspaper and the new cabinet |
| ![Top 5 cities](docs/screenshots/top5.png) | ![Civilization score](docs/screenshots/score.png) |
| The Top 5 cities | The Civilization score |

## Build

    make civ

The original game is not part of this repository.  Put its files (`CIV.EXE`, `ISOUND.CVL`,
the `*.PIC`, `*.PAL`, `*.TXT` files, `FONTS.CV`, ...) in `~/Dos/Civ1` (or point
`$CIV_ORIG`, or `make ORIG=dir`, at them).  The game reads its pictures, fonts and texts from
there.  The first build also extracts three data files from them once (the rule tables, the
starting game state and the sounds: `src/rules_data.c`, `src/fresh_save.c`,
`src/sdl/sound_data.c`); this needs python3 with the `unicorn` module.

Needs a C99 compiler and SDL2 (the Makefile also uses a local `.toolchain/` if present).
On macOS: `xcode-select --install` and `brew install sdl2`, then `make civ` (SDL2 is found
with `sdl2-config`).  Copy the project without `.toolchain/`, which holds Linux binaries.

## Play

    ./civ [--data ~/Dos/Civ1] [--saves save] [--scale 3]

`--data` is the directory with the original files (`*.PIC`, `*.PAL`, `*.TXT`, `FONTS.CV`;
default `$CIV_ORIG`, else `~/Dos/Civ1`); games are saved to `--saves` (default `save/`), and
the saved games in the data directory can be loaded too.  The `.SVE`/`.MAP` files are the original formats.

Keys: numeric keypad / arrows move (Home, PgUp, End, PgDn diagonals); `b` build city,
`f` fortify, `s` sentry, `w` wait, space skip, `r` road, `i` irrigate, `m` mine,
`p` clean pollution, `u` unload, `h` home city, `g` GoTo, Shift-`D` disband, Shift-`P` pillage,
`c` centre the view, Enter on a city opens it.  Esc opens the GAME menu (tax rates, find city,
options, save, revolution, quit); F1–F10 are the advisors and world reports; the mouse works
on the menu bar, the map (click a neighbouring square to move there, a city to open it) and
the minimap.  In the city screen: click squares to move workers, click specialists to change
them, `c`/CHANGE, `b`/BUY, `v` to view the city, click an improvement to sell it.

Sound is the original PC-speaker music and effects (switch it off with Sound in the
GAME menu's Options).

## Test

    make test       # differential tests against the original EXE run in an emulator
                    # (needs python3 with unicorn)
    make smoke      # the SDL front end plays scripted games without a window

GitHub runs only a compile check (`.github/workflows/build.yml`, Linux and macOS): without
the original's files it builds with empty stand-ins for the derived data (`make stub-data`,
`ci/stubs/`), which compiles but does not play.  Run the tests locally before pushing.

# Scorched Earth v1.50

"The Mother of All Games" — the classic DOS artillery game (1995), reverse-engineered and rebuilt for the web.

### [Play now at scorched-earth.berrry.app](https://scorched-earth.berrry.app)

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Mobile |
|--------|----------|--------|
| Adjust angle | Left/Right arrows | D-pad |
| Adjust power | Up/Down arrows | D-pad |
| Cycle weapon | Tab | WPN button |
| Fire | Space | FIRE button |
| Confirm | Enter | OK button |

Fullscreen: click the toggle button on the canvas, or use "START FULLSCREEN" from the landing page. On mobile, fullscreen auto-locks to landscape orientation.

## Project Structure

```
web/              Web reimplementation (pure HTML/CSS/JS, no dependencies)
  index.html      Game page with touch controls and fullscreen support
  css/style.css   Responsive layout, mobile landscape, fullscreen mode
  js/             Game modules (physics, rendering, AI, weapons, etc.)
earth/            Original DOS game files (gitignored, see below)
disasm/           Decoded disassembly and analysis intermediate files
  fpu_decode.py   Borland INT 34h-3Dh FPU instruction decoder
REVERSE.md   Master RE document with all findings
```

## Obtaining the Original Game Binary

The `earth/` directory is gitignored and must be populated manually for reverse engineering work.

**Scorched Earth v1.50** (1995) is freely distributed shareware by Wendell Hicken. To obtain it:

1. Download from [My Abandonware](https://www.myabandonware.com/game/scorched-earth-192) (598 KB DOS archive)
2. Extract the archive into the `earth/` directory
3. Verify: `earth/SCORCH.EXE` should be 415,456 bytes with a 0x6A00 byte MZ header

The key file for RE work is `SCORCH.EXE` (Borland C++ 1993, MZ DOS format). Use with `disasm/fpu_decode.py` to decode the Borland FPU emulation layer (INT 34h-3Dh):

```bash
python3 disasm/fpu_decode.py earth/SCORCH.EXE 0x24F01 0x2610F -c -f
```

See `REVERSE.md` for full binary layout, data structures, and decoded algorithms.

## Running Locally

No build step required. Serve the `web/` directory with any static HTTP server:

```bash
cd web && python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then open `http://localhost:8000`.

## License

The web reimplementation code is open source. The original Scorched Earth binary and assets are property of Wendell Hicken (shareware).

# Airborne Ranger — C port / decompilation

A C port of the DOS game *Airborne Ranger* (MicroProse, 1987), produced by
lifting `AR.EXE` + its `TANDYSND.EXE` overlay through a masm2c-style
translator and hand-verifying the result against the reference binary.
SDL2 frontend; the guest CPU registers/flags and 1MB flat memory model live
in `port/` alongside generated sources in `port/gen/` and the lifted tree in
`lifted/`.

## Bring your own copy

**No original game files are distributed** — not in this repo, not in release
artifacts. To run the port, supply your own DOS copy of the game:

- **Linux/SDL2**: `make -C port` then run `./port/ar_port` from the directory
  containing the game files (`*.DTX`, `*.DAT`, `*.MIJ`, `*.EXE`).
- **Windows x64**: `tools/build_windows.sh` (MinGW cross-build) — or grab the
  release zip and drop the game files next to `ar_port.exe`.
- **Android (TV)**: `sh android/fetch-sdl.sh && gradle -p android
  assembleDebug`; the APK imports your files on first launch (folder picker
  or `adb push`). Remote/gamepad key mapping is built in.

Regenerating the port pipeline (`port/memimg.c`, `port/gen/`,
`port/data_syms.h`) needs the original binaries locally —
`tools/gen_port.py` reads `AR_rebuilt.exe`, `AR.EXE.map`, `AR.EXE.lst`.

Asset tools (work on your own copies, nothing bundled):
`tools/dtx2png.py` decodes DOS `.DTX` art; `tools/dat2png.py` decodes
Atari ST / Amiga `.DAT` + `.ST` graphics (title/combat screens with
palette, planar sprite sheets); `tools/snd2wav.py` extracts the Amiga
`.snd` containers' embedded 8SVX samples to WAV.

The Amiga title music (`armdat.snd` sequenced bank + `armdrv.snd` 68k
Paula player) exists as a standard SoundTracker module — any `.stk`/.mod
player (e.g. `openmpt123 airborne_ranger.stk`, or `openmpt123 --render`
for WAV) plays it; its six instruments match `armdat.snd` byte-for-byte.
ST/Amiga Ghidra decompiles (reading aid, not compiled): see
`/home/xor/ghidra/ar_st/NOTES.md` and `/home/xor/ghidra/ar_amiga/NOTES.md`.

## Controls

arrows = move, Enter / KP5 / Ins = fire & confirm, Esc = back/menu,
digits = weapon select, `+`/`-` = throttle. Gamepads: A=fire, B=back,
dpad/stick=move, LB/RB=−/+.

Env: `M2C_GOD=1` god mode,
`M2C_KEYS`/`M2C_KEYS_DELAY` scripted input (see `port/tests/e2e.sh`).

## CI

`.github/workflows/`: `ci.yml` (build + tests + e2e), `android.yml`,
`windows.yml` (artifacts), `release.yml` (`v*` tag → GitHub release with
APK + Windows zip), `wasm.yml` (experimental skeleton).

# DuckTales Amiga reconstruction

This workspace recovers the original Amiga DuckTales game as readable source
whose behavior we can trust, as the foundation for a later native SDL3 port.
Exact matching decompilation, verified against the immutable original
executable with the pinned Aztec C toolchain, is the preferred recovery and
verification technique. No independent game build exists yet.

Start with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and [the current state and priorities](docs/NEXT.md).
[The vision](docs/VISION.md) and [proof policy](docs/proof-levels.md) define the
goal and what each proof category claims.

The active authorities are:

- `src/` for reconstructed source;
- `recovery/ledger.json`, with its referenced proofs and unit inputs, for
  ownership and acceptance;
- `evidence/fixture-lock.json` for original input identity;
- `docs/blockers.json` for current blockers;
- `docs/toolchain.json` and `toolchain/` for pinned compiler assumptions.

Generated measurements are in `docs/progress.json`. [Whole-image
accounting](docs/ACCOUNTING.md) keeps every unreconstructed byte visible as
RAW_ORACLE_DEBT, and `tools/behavior.py` reports the same evidence by behavior:
what is exact, what is assembly or runtime library, what is unresolved, and
which platform services game code uses.

```powershell
python tools/behavior.py
python tools/readable.py      # readable view with reviewed names -> build/readable/
python tools/grinder.py facts ov04_F_0536
python tools/census.py --check
python tools/hybrid_image.py --check
python -m pytest -n 16 --dist=loadscope -m "not regression_serial" tests
python -m pytest -m regression_serial tests
```

The local immutable disks in `assets/` and installed historical tools are not
tracked. Analysis needs Python and native Capstone. Historical compilation uses
the existing unattended WinUAE worker (see [worker setup](docs/build-worker.md)).
Scratch, compiler caches and worker directories belong under ignored `build/`.
Canonical re-derivation reads `build/compile-cache` and `build/worker-jobs`, so do
not prune them. Retired material goes to `to_delete/` with a manifest entry.

# Stunt Car Racer — browser reconstruction

A playable Three.js/WebGL reconstruction using your supplied Amiga disk and DOS `original/Stunt.img`. The **PHYSICS** selector chooses original Amiga 68000 or DOS x86 player code running in WebAssembly. Three.js renders interpolated views between native updates. The artwork and track renderer use assets decoded from `original/Stunt_Car_Racer_1989_MicroStyle_cr_QTX.adf`; the DOS track data agrees with the Amiga geometry. The browser integration and extraction tools were written for this project. External remakes and disassemblies were consulted as format guides; their source, compiled games, track files, and artwork are not part of this game's build.

## Run

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. `npm run build` produces a standalone static site in `dist/`; `npm run preview` serves that build. The game has no CDN or external service dependency. WebAssembly, WebGL2 and Web Audio are required. Rendering follows the display refresh rate, including 120 Hz on a compatible display; each physics version retains its native timestep (Amiga: 0.12 seconds; DOS: 0.054921875 seconds at the selected original calibration).

### GitHub Pages

Play at **https://jamescarruthers.github.io/stunt_car_racer/**.

The [Pages workflow](.github/workflows/pages.yml) installs locked dependencies with Node.js 22, runs the test suite, builds with the `/stunt_car_racer/` base path, and deploys `dist/` after each push to `main`. Pull requests run the tests and build. You can also run the workflow manually from the repository's Actions tab. The repository's **Settings → Pages → Source** is **GitHub Actions**.

To check the same deployment path locally:

```sh
npm run build -- --base=/stunt_car_racer/
node tools/browser-check.mjs --production --base-path=/stunt_car_racer/ --boost-only
```

The workflow follows the [Vite deployment guide](https://vite.dev/guide/static-deploy.html#github-pages) and [GitHub Pages workflow documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages). The deployed site contains the game and dependency licence files; the repository also contains the original disks, extraction tools and physics verification fixtures.

## Playing

**DOS is the default** when no physics preference is saved. Use **PHYSICS → AMIGA / DOS** in the header to change version. The choice persists after reload, including existing Amiga selections. Switching during a race restarts that same track with the selected physics; lap records are separate for each version. The graphics option is independent.

Choose **Practice**, select one of the eight tracks, then start. **Start a season** shows the original driver portraits and current division lineup before racing rivals across four divisions. **Drivers / Divisions** also opens this page from the main menu. A season awards two points for winning and one for the fastest lap, with promotion/relegation after four player races. Progress and lap records are saved in this browser.

| Control | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys / WASD | Accelerate, brake/reverse, steer |
| Space / Shift | Boost / release the crane |
| R | Crane recovery |
| G / 3D button | Switch between original pixelation and full-resolution 3D |
| P | Pause/resume |
| Escape | Return to menu |
| M / F | Mute / fullscreen |
| Enter / arrow keys | Select / navigate menus |

The throttle stays open until braking, as in the original. Touch controls appear on devices with a coarse pointer. A standard gamepad uses its left stick, right/left triggers, and A button. Switching away from the window pauses the race.

After recovery, **press Space to release the crane**. The original lift, swing and drop are now simulated. At **Little Ramp**, reverse for a run-up before accelerating with boost. About five seconds holding Down, then Up + Space, clears the jump in the recovery regression. The original also needs a run-up from this drop point. Space can boost braking/reversing when held with Down.

## Fidelity

**Directly extracted:** all eight track bytecode streams, section templates, horizontal coordinates, height profiles, banking, track names, boost allowances, division track assignments, 11 driver names, nine bitmap screens, both bitmap fonts, the expanded Amiga palette, the horizon geometry, and eight PCM samples. Track vertices retain the original coordinate values; the renderer converts X/Z by 1/32 and Y by 1/128. All 445 section joins agree within one original coordinate unit. The display is 320×200 with a 4:3 presentation, nearest pixel scaling and flat polygon colours.

**Executed from your disk:** player controls and latched throttle, standard/super engine forces, boost consumption, three wheel suspension, grip, steering, all linear/angular integration, jumps and landings, track lookup, crane selection and motion, drawbridge heights, collision impulses and damage/crack calculations. The browser loads the unchanged 408,540-byte payload at its original address into a Musashi 68000 emulator. Only Amiga input polling, audio output and bitmap text output are replaced with browser boundaries. Physics instructions and fixed-point arithmetic are unchanged.

**DOS execution:** the browser verifies and loads the unchanged 105,856-byte code/data extract from `CAR.EGA`, applies the executable’s 45 original MZ relocations and calls its x86 routines. Native steering, suspension, integration, controls, boost, track lookup, bridge and crane routines match the extracted reference traces. DOS collision, automatic recovery and damage routines are also connected; the damage calculation reads and writes private EGA planes initialized with 32,000 original cockpit bytes. Three.js continues to display the Amiga artwork.

**Browser presentation and race flow:** Three.js rendering, camera placement, visible instruments and effects, menus, lap/season bookkeeping, rival driving policy and sound playback remain browser implementations. Rival positions are converted into original road coordinates for the native collision routines. Original damage logic retains offscreen cockpit bitplanes. The first crane drop releases automatically; later recoveries wait for Space. Manual recovery and automatic recovery use the native restart routine. This is a player-physics execution port, not a complete Amiga/DOS machine emulator or full race-loop emulation.

The **3D** button (or **G**, including in fullscreen) switches between the original 320×200 rendering and full-resolution 3D at the display's pixel density. The choice is saved locally and can be changed during a race. Original cockpit and menu bitmap artwork retains its pixel detail in either mode.

The cockpit displays the original animated front-wheel sprites, with independent heights driven by each native engine's suspension state. Off-road ground contact produces the original eight dust-cloud sprites. Artwork, wheel-height lookup, dust frame order and sprite offsets come from the supplied Amiga disk; wheel rotation timing and particle animation are browser presentation adaptations. Both physics modes use these effects, which freeze while paused and clear during crane recovery.

**Timing:** Amiga physics executes once every six PAL frames (0.12 seconds). DOS uses the original calibration routine with coefficient `0x646f` and its native clock increment of `0.054921875` seconds (about 18.2 updates/second). DOS originally adapts to CPU speed; this chooses its original minimum coefficient consistently across browsers. Car/camera poses, the rival and moving bridge vertices interpolate between completed states on `requestAnimationFrame`. Interpolation does not change CPU memory or collision geometry, and pause freezes both simulation and interpolation. This keeps the original input/physics cadence and adds up to one original tick of presentation latency. Full-resolution 3D remains independently selectable.

**Amiga verification:** the same WebAssembly binary shipped to the browser reproduces the independent Unicorn recordings: all acceleration/braking/free-fall/jump samples, 1,134 steering cases, suspension and grip probes, plus **5,600 gameplay updates across all eight tracks and both leagues with byte-for-byte agreement in the recorded physics state**. That includes finite boost, damage, crane phases, recovery and mutable bridge profiles. Tests at 30/60/120/144 display updates per second reach identical native states. Additional checks cover bank orientation, interpolation, recovery and native rival contact.

**DOS verification:** all **25,424 recorded updates** across all eight tracks, both leagues and two original CPU calibrations agree byte for byte over the entire 64 KiB data segment with the independent native Unicorn recordings. Integration checks cover settled suspension, both steering directions, banking, bridge geometry, native recovery, the Little Ramp reverse run-up, rival collisions, crack/wreck logic, and identical simulation at 30/60/120/144 Hz rendering. The production browser check exercises switching both ways, persistence, both resolutions, all tracks, both race modes, pause and interpolation.

Full Amiga/DOS boot/hardware, the original AI and complete race-loop parity remain unverified. Serial multiplayer, original disk saves and the crack intro are not implemented. See the [current execution audit](analysis/FORMAT.md#browser-execution-of-the-original-physics) for the exact boundaries. The former continuous JavaScript solver is archived in `tools/reference-physics.js` solely for historical regression comparisons; it is not imported into gameplay.

## Reproduce the extraction

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
npm run extract
npm test
npm run build
```

`tools/extract_original.py` reads only the supplied disk. It identifies the Quartex plaintext payload at disk offset `0xDC00`, validates its entry signature, and extracts 408,540 bytes with original load address `0xE700`. Unsupported disk variants fail rather than silently producing substitute content.

- `public/assets/manifest.json`: disk/payload SHA-256 and asset source ranges with hashes.
- `analysis/original.bin` and `public/assets/original-code.bin`: identical, unmodified extracted payloads. The browser verifies the latter against the manifest before executing it.
- `analysis/original-68000.asm`: Capstone linear disassembly of executable regions, generated from that payload. It includes data and unresolved protection placeholders; it is not a fully annotated or reassemblable source recovery.
- `analysis/FORMAT.md`: decoded data formats and known implementation differences.
- `analysis/dos/REPORT.md`: inspection of the supplied `original/Stunt.img`, including the decoded DOS executable, shared track data, native recovery checks and CPU calibration findings. Reproduce with `python3 tools/inspect-dos.py` and the optional Unicorn harness `tools/probe-dos.py`.
- `analysis/dos/PHYSICS.md` and `analysis/dos/dos-physics.zip`: runnable DOS player-physics extraction, native code/data, API, disassembly and verification. Build with `python3 tools/extract-dos-physics.py` before running the DOS probes. The extraction script also publishes `public/assets/dos-physics.bin`, `dos-physics.json` and `dos-cockpit.bin` for the browser.
- `tools/probe-original.py`, `analysis/original-physics-traces.json` and `analysis/original-runtime-traces.json`: independent Unicorn measurements from the disk. Use `--runtime-only --output analysis/original-runtime-traces.json` to reproduce the extended gameplay fixtures.
- `src/original-machine.js`, `src/dos-machine.js`, `src/original-car.js`: the two native CPU adapters and shared race bookkeeping.
- `src/simulation-clock.js`: fixed native tick and render interpolation.
- `src/cockpit-effects.js`, `public/assets/cockpit-sprites.png` and `cockpit-effects.json`: original wheel/dust artwork and presentation data. Check both physics modes with `node tools/browser-check.mjs --production --presentation-only`.
- `tests/emulated-physics.test.js`, `tests/dos-physics.test.js`: current original-code parity and integration checks. Other test files retain the preceding continuous-solver audit, alongside asset/track/season checks.
- `tools/browser-check.mjs`: Chrome smoke check and screenshots; run against the dev server with `node tools/browser-check.mjs`. Use `node tools/browser-check.mjs --production` to serve and test the packaged `dist/` build. Set `CHROME_PATH` if Chrome is installed elsewhere.

Format guides: [Vesuri's Amiga disassembly](https://github.com/Vesuri/stuntcarracer), [StuntCarRemake reference material](https://github.com/ptitSeb/stuntcarremake). Browser engine: [Three.js](https://threejs.org/). Generic CPU dependency: [Musashi WebAssembly](https://github.com/mblsha/musashi-wasm), pinned to `musashi-wasm@0.1.31`; it supplies no game code or data. Its [copyright notice](public/licenses/MUSASHI.txt) is included in the static build.

DOS CPU dependency: [Unicorn.js](https://github.com/AlexAltea/unicorn.js) / [Unicorn 2.1.4](https://github.com/unicorn-engine/unicorn/tree/2.1.4), built with Emscripten 4.0.15. The upstream browser helper adapter leaked temporary TCG registers and crashed on long x86 blocks. Our build frees those temporary registers after emitting each helper call; game instructions are untouched. The [GPLv2 licence](public/licenses/UNICORN.txt) and [complete corresponding patched source and rebuild instructions](public/licenses/unicorn-source.tar.gz) ship with the static site. `src/vendor/unicorn-x86.mjs` is loaded only when DOS is selected.

Original game and its assets: Geoff Crammond / MicroStyle, 1989; rights remain with their respective owners. Three.js, Musashi, Unicorn and the development dependencies retain their own licences.

Goal: a modern portable C + SDL port that is behaviourally faithful to `orig/CIV.EXE`
and loads the original assets from `orig/`. Work proceeds in milestones.

## CIV.EXE facts

- Microsoft C 5.x ("MS Run-Time Library - Copyright (c) 1988"), large model, MS LINK overlays,
  then EXEPACKed. Unpacked: 199,776-byte root image, 2,517 relocations, plus 126,401 bytes of
  appended overlay data (~23 overlays, entered through `int 3Fh` thunks — 147 in the root).
- Roughly 350 `push bp; mov bp,sp` functions in the root and ~150 in overlays, plus hand-written asm.
- Real entry `2058:2E83`. DGROUP = segment `0x2A1B` (file offset `0x2A1B0` in the root image).
- 31 root code segments (from relocation targets) plus DGROUP. Overlays are 23 small MZ images
  appended at file offset `0x2B800`; all are linked at segment `0x2388` and loaded into an empty
  9,648-byte buffer there. Calls into overlays are inline `int 3Fh; db overlay; dw offset`.
- Graphics, sound and misc helpers are separate driver binaries loaded at runtime:
  `EGRAPHIC/MGRAPHIC/TGRAPHIC.EXE` (EGA/MCGA/Tandy), `MISC.EXE`, `*SOUND.CVL`.

### DGROUP tables (offsets from DS)

| Offset | Contents | Record |
|-------:|----------|--------|
| `0x00AC` | government names (6) | NUL-separated strings |
| `0x00E5` | trade goods (8) | strings |
| `0x0239` | leader titles per government (6) | strings |
| `0x0282` | terrain + specials (24) | 19 B: name[12], move, defense×2, food, shields, trade, ?, ega colour |
| `0x04DA` | advances (72) | 22 B: name[20], prereq1, prereq2 (signed byte; -1 none, 127 never) |
| `0x0B9A` | buildings & wonders (46) | 30 B: name[24], cost/10, upkeep, prereq (words) |
| `0x112A` | unit types (28) | 34 B: name[12], 11 words (see `src/rules.h`) |
| `0x14D8` | civilizations (16) | 58 B: 5 words, leader[16], plural[16], adjective[16] |

### PIC / PAL format

A file is a series of chunks: `tag[2] length[u16] data[length]`.

- `E0` — 256-byte EGA dither map (`first, last, map[]`).
- `M0` — VGA palette: `first, last`, then 6-bit RGB triples for `first..last`.
- `X0` — 8-bit image to end of file: `width u16, height u16, maxbits u8`, then an LZW stream
  whose output is RLE-decoded (`0x90 n`: n=0 → literal 0x90, else repeat previous byte n-1 more times).
  (`X1` would be the same with 4-bit packed pixels; none seen yet.)

The LZW is **not** textbook: it mirrors the routine at root `0x1219–0x13B3`. It adds a dictionary
entry for *every* code (including the first after a reset, using the stale previous code), widens
when the next code exceeds the mask, and resets when the width would exceed `maxbits` (≤ 11).
All 106 `.PIC` files in `orig/` decode to 320×200.

### Save files

`.SVE` (37,856 bytes) is a raw dump of 80 globals in a fixed order with no header; the order and
sizes come from the serializer `o_11_09e4`, and `src/save.c` reproduces it. Layout highlights:
`0x0000` turn, `0x0002` human civ, `0x0006` world seed, `0x0008` year, `0x000A` difficulty,
`0x0010` leader/civ/adjective names, `0x0138` treasury, `0x04E8` advance bitsets,
`0x1508` cities (128 × 28 B), `0x2308` unit-type table (the game saves its own copy),
`0x26C0` units (8 civs × 128 × 12 B), `0x6970` city names (256 × 13 B).

`.MAP` is a 320×200 `X0` picture: the off-screen page that holds the world. See the layer table in
`src/game.h`. Special resources and huts are not stored; both come from a hash of the square's
4×4 block and the world seed (`has_special_resource`, `has_hut` in `src/map.c`).

## Porting conventions

- Behaviour must match the original exactly, including its bugs; each reproduced bug carries a
  `sic`/"the original ..." comment. Where the original reads memory that does not exist in the
  port (indexing past an array), the port uses the constant data the EXE has there when that is
  knowable (e.g. `civ_types[-1]`), otherwise 0, with a comment.
- 16-bit arithmetic is reproduced with `int16_t` casts where products can overflow.
- User interface is reached only through `ui.h`; `ui_headless.c` answers dialogs with the first
  option, as the oracle's stubbed dialog engine does.
- Functions not ported yet are in `src/todo.c` and abort if reached.
- Display code that consumes random numbers is part of the game state: redrawing the map view
  (`view_center`, f_1b05_0004) draws `rnd(256)`, and whether it is redrawn depends on the view
  position (`view_follow`, f_0860_1679), so both live in `src/view.c`, not behind `ui.h`.
  The newspaper (overlay 21) and city view (overlay 19) also draw random numbers; the oracle
  stubs them for now, so the port does not model them yet.
- Where the original reads uninitialised memory, the port picks a definition and the oracle
  is patched to do the same (`UNDEFINED_PATCHES` in `tests/run.py`).  So far: the transport
  code of `ai_unit_command` reads `city[l12]` with `l12` never set; the port uses the nearest
  city.  Where the original never terminates (a stack ring broken by `unit_unlink`'s handling
  of ships leaving a shared square makes the transport cargo walk loop for ever), the port
  bails out after 1000 steps and the test skips that case.
- Reads past the end of tables use `dgroup_init` (the EXE's initialised DGROUP, generated into
  `rules_data.c`) via `dgroup_word()`, e.g. unit-type fields of a deleted unit (type 255/-1).
- `tools/dsfield.py 0xf5b8 ...` names the saved field at a DGROUP offset.
- Some of the original's random numbers depend on the player's timing: animations that run
  until a key is pressed draw random numbers (the spaceship screen's stars, the talking
  leader in diplomacy dialogs).  The engine provides these as calls the front end makes per
  frame (`spaceship_stars_step`); their count cannot match a given playthrough of the
  original, only the logic can.
- The city view (overlay 19) re-seeds the random generator from the sum of the city name's
  characters and lays the city out with it; the newspaper (overlay 21) draws its crowd, name
  and headline at random.  Both are modelled in the engine (view.c); the oracle runs the
  original entry points up to their last random number and jumps to their epilogue

  oracle as "no section chosen" (straight to its final `redraw_map`), which is what the
  headless UI answers.

# `gamedata/` — the original DOS game packs

`gamedata/` holds unmodified installs of the original DOS Lemmings games —
one directory per game pack, straight off the original floppies/CD, byte-
for-byte as shipped. Nothing in here is edited; every asset this project
derives from it (real level terrain, sprites, sounds, and now menu
graphics) comes from decoding these files, never hand-editing them.
